body: Infrastructure as a service (IaaS) is the most flexible cloud service category and gives maximum control. You essentially rent hardware in a cloud datacenter, and what you do with it is up to you. The provider handles the physical infrastructure, internet connectivity and physical security. You handle operating system installation, configuration and maintenance, network configuration, database and storage configuration, and patching. Typical scenarios are lift-and-shift migration and quickly creating development and test environments.
author: claude

body: Platform as a service (PaaS) is a middle ground between renting datacenter space (IaaS) and paying for a complete solution (SaaS). The provider maintains the physical infrastructure, operating systems, middleware, development tools and analytics services, so you do not license or patch operating systems and databases. You focus on your application code, data and access controls. Some networking and application security settings are shared. Typical scenarios are a development framework, and analytics or business intelligence.
author: claude

body: Software as a service (SaaS) is the most complete cloud service model: you rent or use a fully developed application. It is the easiest to get running and needs the least technical expertise, but may be the least flexible. The provider manages almost the whole stack, including infrastructure, platform and application maintenance. You primarily manage your data, identity and access settings, and device access. SaaS has the lowest operational overhead. Common examples are email and messaging, productivity apps, and finance and expense tracking.
author: claude

body: Choose the service type by how much control you need. IaaS gives the most control and suits lift-and-shift migration and rapidly replicating test and development environments. PaaS suits developers who want a framework with built-in scalability and high availability, and teams doing analytics or business intelligence. SaaS suits ready-made needs such as email, messaging, productivity and finance tracking, with the least work for you but the least flexibility.
